title: Cooking with Codex — Charlie Guo & Gabriel Chua, OpenAI
talk_summary: The transferable core is orchestration patterns for long autonomous runs: verifiable success criteria, goal files + progress dashboards, sub-agent context isolation, deterministic hooks, and timer-driven polling automations.

takeaways.technique: Goal file + progress dashboard for long runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one monolithic prompt, Codex writes a goals.md with a series of milestones and a progress dashboard.html, then spawns separate threads per milestone that audit against the goal file and nudge the main thread back on track when it deviates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't create one goal create a series of goals and put it in a goals.mmuckdown file ... create a dashboard, progress dashboard.html

takeaways.technique: Sub-agents for context isolation, threads for visibility
takeaways.what_they_do: Sub-agents keep context separate and only report results back to the parent (delegation invisible to user); thread-to-thread handoff is used when a human wants to watch the exchange. Sub-agent configs (prompt, model tier) live in per-agent TOML files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sub agents are one where uh, you know, you're keeping the context separate and the mo the the models are communicating with each other

takeaways.technique: Remote-to-local thread handoff for browser QA
takeaways.what_they_do: A remote (cloud) thread messages a local thread to run Chrome-extension click-through QA, then the local thread sends results back; the remote agent can't reach the browser itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the remote thread can communicate with the local thread and says hey you got to do click ops you got to do browser you got to do QA testing

takeaways.what_they_do: Hooks in config run deterministic scripts at turn end or before tool calls: tidy repo, lint, scan for leaked API keys, whitelist-check tools, custom output validation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at the every end of its turn a Python script to just tidy the repo ... you can run it deterministically with a hook

takeaways.what_they_do: When waiting on slow external events (droplet provisioning, CI), the agent creates a timer automation that re-checks every 5 minutes and resumes the task when ready, instead of blocking or idling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I set a codeex heartbeat to resume this track in about 5 minutes ... Is it ready? Is it ready?

takeaways.what_they_do: A scheduled automation reads a Slack channel, classifies messages (compliment/bug/feature), and for bugs/features spawns a worktree thread that opens a PR and requests review, with reminders if unapproved.
